ip_top_stories.title: Authors Sue Meta's AI Scientists Directly in Llama Copyright Case
ip_top_stories.summary: Authors have expanded their copyright lawsuit against Meta by suing the company's AI scientists directly in connection with the Llama large language model. The move represents a notable legal escalation, targeting individual researchers rather than solely the corporation. The case centres on allegations that Meta's AI systems were trained on copyrighted works without authorisation.

ip_top_stories.title: UMG and Sony seek to add over 61k recordings to Suno lawsuit after discovery reveals AI trained on 'millions' of their copyrighted tracks
ip_top_stories.summary: Universal Music Group and Sony Music are seeking to dramatically expand their copyright lawsuit against AI music generator Suno, adding over 61,000 recordings after discovery proceedings allegedly revealed that Suno's AI was trained on millions of their copyrighted tracks without a licence. The move signals an aggressive litigation strategy by major labels to broaden the scope of damages. The case is closely watched as a bellwether for music industry claims against generative AI companies.

ip_top_stories.title: Sony Music Files to Expand Udio Suit, Alleges 30K Infringed Works
ip_top_stories.summary: Sony Music has filed to expand its copyright lawsuit against AI music generator Udio, alleging infringement across approximately 30,000 works. The expansion follows a pattern of major rights holders broadening their legal claims against AI audio platforms. The case adds to the mounting legal pressure facing generative AI music services.

ip_top_stories.title: AI Firms Can't Shake Disney, WB's Copyright Suit
ip_top_stories.summary: A US court has refused to dismiss copyright infringement claims brought by Disney and Warner Bros. against AI firms including MiniMax, allowing the case to proceed. The ruling is a significant setback for AI defendants seeking early dismissal of major studio copyright actions. The case concerns allegations that AI systems were trained on or used to reproduce copyrighted film and television content.

ip_top_stories.title: Eisner Awards to Implement AI Policy Following Controversy
ip_top_stories.summary: The Eisner Awards will introduce an AI disclosure policy after a nominated anthology was withdrawn amid controversy over AI-generated content. The Stardust anthology's removal highlighted growing tensions in the comics industry over AI-assisted creative work and its eligibility for awards recognition. The new policy signals that major industry bodies are beginning to formalise standards around AI content.

ip_further_links.title: Artist Sues Copyright Office Over its Refusal to Register His AI-Enhanced Photo
ip_further_links.summary: An artist has filed a lawsuit against the US Copyright Office after it declined to register a photograph he enhanced using AI tools, raising questions about where human authorship ends and AI assistance begins under copyright law.

ip_further_links.title: Can you own a voice? Taylor Swift's latest legal move raises big questions for AI and copyright
ip_further_links.summary: Taylor Swift's legal action over AI voice cloning is prompting wider debate about whether existing copyright and trademark frameworks are adequate to protect performers' vocal identities from AI replication.

ip_further_links.title: Europe's Copyright Trap Stalls AI Ambitions - Center for European Policy Analysis (CEPA)
ip_further_links.summary: CEPA argues that Europe's current copyright framework is creating regulatory friction that is hampering AI development, as unresolved text and data mining rules leave AI companies uncertain about the legality of training on copyrighted material.

ip_further_links.title: Japan eyes rules to regulate AI summaries' 'free riding' on news
ip_further_links.summary: Japan is considering new regulations to prevent AI services from free-riding on news publishers' content by generating summaries without compensation or licensing agreements.

ip_further_links.title: Media orgs push back against the relaxation of federal government's stance on AI, copyright
ip_further_links.summary: US media organisations are resisting moves by the federal government to soften its position on AI and copyright, arguing that weaker protections would undermine publishers and rights holders.

ip_further_links.title: Australian creatives urge the government to 'hold the line' on AI and copyright law
ip_further_links.summary: Australian creative industry groups are calling on the government to resist pressure to introduce AI copyright exceptions, warning that weakening protections would harm local creators.

ip_further_links.title: Legal Risk Could Deflate the GenAI Bubble
ip_further_links.summary: Analysis argues that accumulating copyright litigation and unresolved licensing questions pose a material legal risk that could significantly deflate valuations and investment in the generative AI sector.

ip_further_links.title: The User Has Changed. Has Scholarly Publishing?
ip_further_links.summary: The Scholarly Kitchen examines how AI-driven changes in researcher behaviour are challenging scholarly publishers to rethink discovery, access, and the value they provide to users.

ip_further_links.title: Can you trademark identity? The new legal strategy celebrities are using against AI
ip_further_links.summary: Celebrities and their legal teams are increasingly exploring trademark and right-of-publicity claims as a strategy to combat unauthorised AI reproductions of their likenesses and personas.

ip_further_links.title: How Italy's SIAE Is Shaping the Future of Copyright Protection Amid AI
ip_further_links.summary: Italy's collecting society SIAE is taking an active role in shaping national and European policy on AI and copyright, pushing for stronger protections and mandatory licensing frameworks for AI training.
